doc.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024

title: Tuning and South African sound
summary: Discussion of sharp intonation as part of the sound, and how it fits big band charts versus African music.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: I’m so glad you brought that up. Because I was going to ask this and I was trying to figure out how to ask it.

But I’ve wondered if it’s been my imagination that when I listen to some West African but South African music, I hear as if their guitars are tuned slightly different and they may — the horn players may play a little sharp, or just there’s something there and I can’t quite figure it out, but it’s part of the sound.

It’s part of the sound. And again, my ethnomusicology background made that okay with me or as I’ve brought in other people to do workshops and they say, “Wow, you know, your kids play with a lot of soul but you know I just wish they’d play in tune.” And that was a thing, and sometimes I felt the same way and sometimes I didn’t. It depends on context. Have you ever conducted a big band? A student big band?

If you’re doing a Neal Hefti chart and the sax section is sharp, it’s not going to sound good. But if on the other hand you played a chart that would be somebody’s transcription of the African Jazz Pioneers, which was a terrific small big band back in the day, and they were trained like the musicians I interacted with a lot in England, you know to — you know they’d have their small group gigs but they’d be in the Ronnie Scott’s All- Stars, they’d be in the BBC Big Band, they came up through the National Jazz Orchestra. So they’d nail the parts and play them exactly in tune. This is fictional. It didn’t actually happen. But I’m sure that would just sound wrong. It isn’t how the music was conceived in the first place.
Did it have anything to do with the music in the townships, if that is a correct term to use,
Was it keyboard based or was it more guitar oriented so that they weren’t concerned with tuning up to A 440. Maybe I’m going too far with this.
